name: Axis Bank Ltd.
business_summary: India's third-largest private-sector bank (retail, SME, corporate, treasury; Rs13.8 lakh cr gross advances at Sep 2026; branches across India plus DIFC and Singapore and a GIFT City unit). Includes subsidiaries Axis Finance, Axis AMC, Axis Securities, Axis Capital and the (Max-linked) Axis Max Life stake (model knowledge). Promoter holding only 7.86%; FIIs 38%, DIIs 44.5%. Q2 FY27 PAT Rs7,003cr standalone (+38% y/y) as provisions fell, but NII growth lagged balance-sheet growth and the shares fell ~4% on the results as costs and fees missed estimates.

exposures.mechanism: Repo +25bp (RBI hiked to 5.50% on 2026-10-07). ~50% of loans repo/EBLR-linked reprice at once while deposits lag, so a transient NIM gain (sell-side: up to ~10bp for large banks) but Axis has the highest term-deposit/FCNR(B) share among top banks and the hike lifts de-rating risk. NIM +4bp on ~Rs17 lakh cr earning assets = Rs680cr/yr = ~2% of PAT; persistence 0.25 -> +0.5; offset by P/E compression from higher discount rate (-1.5) => ~-1.0.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo to 5.50%, stance calibrated tightening (The Hindu / SCC Online)

exposures.mechanism: 10y +25bp: AFS/FVTPL book ~Rs1 lakh cr x mod. duration ~2.5 x 0.25% = ~Rs600cr MTM loss = ~1.5% of annual PAT (persistence 0.25 -> -0.4); cost-of-equity +25bp on a 13x P/E bank ~ -1.6%. Total ~-2. Model-knowledge estimate of investment book size.
+3pp system credit growth lifts Axis advances (already +23% y/y, Rs13.8 lakh cr gross) ~3pp more; NII +3% on constant NIM, opex leverage => PAT +4%; persistence 0.5-0.75 => ~+3.
Deposit growth +3pp eases the LDR/CD-ratio constraint (deposits +21% vs advances +23%) and lowers marginal cost of funds ~3-5bp => NII +1%; plus unconstrained loan growth. ~+2.

+50bp credit cost on Rs13.8 lakh cr advances = Rs6,900cr pre-tax = ~Rs5,200cr post-tax vs TTM PAT Rs30,000cr = -17% EPS; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap ~1 => -8.5. Asset quality currently improving (provisions fell in Q2) so near-term skew is mild.

evidence.note: Q2 PAT +38% to Rs7,003cr (standalone), advances +23%, deposits +21%, NII +12%; missed estimates (Moneycontrol/Fortune India/Reuters)

exposures.mechanism: Unsecured retail (cards, PL) ~Rs1.2 lakh cr (model estimate ~9% of loans): +1pp delinquency x LGD 80% = ~Rs960cr pre-tax = ~2.4% of PAT; persistence 0.5 -> ~-1.2; plus sentiment/sector de-rating => -2.

A tightening step (risk-weights, LCR run-off, ECL transition from FY28, digital-deposit outflow norms) raises capital/liquidity costs; CET1 buffer is comfortable so effect is mainly P/E: ~-2.5 per step.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo to 5.50%, stance calibrated tightening (The Hindu / SCC Online)

exposures.mechanism: FIIs hold 38.05% (down from 42.04% in Mar 2026): +US$5bn/qtr FPI inflow historically lifts large private banks ~2-4% market-adjusted (flow beta); empirical t-stats on market-adjusted macro series are weak so central shrunk to +2.5.
+1pp GDP growth raises credit demand (~1.5x loan elasticity) and lowers credit costs; PAT +3-5%; persistence 0.5-1.0 => +2.5.

Escalation: Brent up (pack: Brent already +49.5% 12m) -> CPI up, INR weaker -> RBI more hawkish (it hiked on 2026-10-07 'amid geopolitical tensions'), risk-off FPI selling of financials. Axis has DIFC/Dubai/Sharjah presence and Gulf NRI deposits. Est. -3.
VIX +5pts => FPI risk-off; Axis beta 1.2-1.26 to Nifty; roughly -1.5% market-adjusted (empirical coefficient for VIX not significant).

Rupee weakness (+3%) triggers FPI outflows and imported inflation, but FCNR(B)-swap-related and Dubai/Singapore assets give small positive translation. Net ~-0.8; low confidence. Q2 NIM was dragged by FCNR(B) inflows (sell-side previews).

current_state.trend: Standalone PAT Rs7,003cr (+38% y/y) helped by lower provisions; gross advances +23% y/y, deposits +21%, NII +12%; NIM under pressure from FCNR(B) inflows and deposit mix; fee income and costs disappointed. Screener consolidated PAT Rs7,666cr flat q/q.
current_state.valuation: P/E 13.2x, P/B ~1.7x (Rs1,275 / BV Rs738); within the 52w range Rs1,150-1,418; stock +1.5% 3m, +4.0% 12m, 1y vol 25%.
